alternates.description: VE Option 1: Mechanically attached system (instead of fully adhered)
VE Option 2: Single-layer R-30 insulation (instead of two-layer staggered)
VE Option 3: Upgrade to 80 mil TPO membrane with 30-year NDL warranty
VE Option 4: Upgrade insulation to R-38
VE Option 5: Combined package (mech-attached + 80 mil + R-38, no cover board)
VE Option 6: Split project across fiscal years for CCA tax treatment (schedule impact)

exclusions_declared: Major steel deck repairs exceeding $10,000 allowance
Major wood deck replacement exceeding $10,000 allowance
Replacement of damaged roof drains or leaders
Work outside standard hours (7 AM - 6 PM weekdays)
Hazardous material abatement beyond minor handling
Third-party testing/inspection beyond our testing allowance
clarifications: Ponding correction: $20,000 tapered insulation allowance; final quantity confirmed during removal
Deck conditions: $10,000 steel + $10,000 wood allowances; major repairs extra
Hazardous materials: testing allowance + minor handling only; major abatement extra
Phasing schedule assumes reasonable tenant cooperation for access and coordination
HVAC coordination: weekday shutdowns require 72-hour notice; weekends preferred
Temperature monitoring equipment to be provided by owner
Cover board included in base bid; can be removed if VE Option 5 selected (per Carlisle/Firestone for mechanically attached systems)
Building permits typically owner responsibility; can be arranged separately

substitutions_proposed.spec_item: Fully adhered TPO membrane attachment (RFP section 3.1)
substitutions_proposed.substitute_offered: VE Option 1 / Option 5: Mechanically attached assembly
substitutions_proposed.equivalence_justification: Bidder states building height (28 ft) and sheltered industrial location make wind uplift risk moderate; mechanically attached widely used in similar applications; same 20-yr NDL available. Does not quote a specific CSA A123.21 / FM 1-29 wind uplift design basis.

substitutions_proposed.spec_item: 1/4 in. gypsum or HD polyiso cover board (RFP scope item)
substitutions_proposed.substitute_offered: VE Option 5: Omit cover board (only with mechanically attached assembly)
substitutions_proposed.equivalence_justification: Bidder states cover board not required with mechanically attached assembly per Carlisle and Firestone manufacturer guidance. No attached manufacturer letter confirming this for 60/80 mil TPO on polyiso in this configuration.

substitutions_proposed.spec_item: R-30 two-layer polyiso with staggered joints (RFP scope item 3)
substitutions_proposed.equivalence_justification: Bidder acknowledges more thermal bridging at joints (5-8 percent energy penalty) and does not recommend it. Non-equivalent; offered for owner consideration only.

materials_system.manufacturer: Carlisle Syntec / Firestone Building Products / GAF (named certifications held; specific TPO manufacturer for this project not explicitly declared in base bid)

materials_system.membrane_thickness_actual: 60 mil (base bid); 80 mil available under VE Option 3 / 5
materials_system.insulation_spec: R-30 polyiso, two-layer staggered joints (base bid)

warranty_offered.evidence_page: Warranty (Base Bid) section, page 3; Manufacturer Certifications section, page 9

technical_approach.narrative: Three-phase installation (office wing, then northwest warehouse, then southeast with ponding correction) over 90 days. Max 10,000 sqft exposed (below 15,000 sqft RFP limit). Daily watertight close-out by 5 PM. Weekend tarp protection. Dedicated phasing coordinator. Bi-weekly progress reports. 72-hour HVAC shutdown notice.
technical_approach.tear_off_staging_plan: Phased tear-off by roof section with complete isolation between phases; daily watertight close-out; max 10,000 sqft open at any time.
technical_approach.weather_protection_plan: Each phase watertight by 5:00 PM daily; weekend protection via reinforced tarps with weighted edges and secondary drainage.
technical_approach.fall_protection_plan: Fall protection training for all workers (updated annually); dedicated safety coordinator for projects over 75,000 sqft; COR certified; CRSP-certified safety coordinator named (Marcus Johnson). No specific anchor point / tie-off strategy for parapets described.
technical_approach.waste_disposal_plan: Daily cleanup and debris removal; legal disposal of removed BUR; lead flashing separated and disposed as hazardous waste; $3,500 testing allowance for suspected ACM; bidder handles up to 100 sqft non-friable ACM under own procedures.

wsib_clearance.evidence: Attachments list: 'WSIB Clearance Certificate' plus 'WSIB Experience Rating Letter (0.81)'; Insurance Coverage section page 8 lists WSIB Account #7890123-45.
wsib_clearance.notes: Certificate date not quoted in body; online re-verification at clearances.wsib.ca will be an award condition added by the recommendation memo (per fixture 04 section 1.4).

cgl_insurance.evidence: Insurance Coverage section, page 8: 'Commercial General Liability: $5,000,000 per occurrence'. COI attached per attachments list. Limit meets RFP $5M minimum exactly.
cgl_insurance.notes: Bid does not confirm owner (Tenebrus Capital) named as additional insured on the COI, does not state completed-operations tail years, and does not confirm the COI named insured matches 'Heritage Construction Group'. Owner must review attached COI to verify these three items before award.

bonding.evidence: Attachments list does not include a bid bond or consent of surety. Body of bid has no bid-bond statement. Bonding capacity declared 'up to $5 million per project' (Why Heritage section, page 9) — at/below a $578K base bid that is adequate, but no named surety. RFP §9.2 requires 50% performance + 50% L&M bonds post-award.
bonding.notes: Bid bond is NOT in the RFP mandatory_requirements (bid_bond_percent unset) nor in §6.2 submission_requirements — cannot be grounds for disqualification at submission (fixture 04 §5; qualification-check SKILL.md §3 applicability rule). Performance/L&M consent-of-surety is a pre-award clarification item, not a submission-stage fail. Owner to obtain written consent of surety for 50% performance + 50% L&M before contract signing.

working_at_heights_training.evidence: Safety Program section, page 8: 'Fall protection training for all workers (updated annually)'; COR certified.
working_at_heights_training.notes: Bid does not cite O. Reg. 297/13 by name but 'updated annually' exceeds the 3-year validity requirement; Ministry-approved WAH training implied by COR certification.

addenda_acknowledgment.evidence: No Form of Tender page quoted in the submitted document; no addenda list acknowledged in the text of the bid.
addenda_acknowledgment.notes: RFP required addenda acknowledgment in Form of Tender. Converted markdown does not include the Form of Tender page; owner should confirm acknowledgment in the submitted PDF before ranking.

non_collusion_declaration.evidence: No non-collusion declaration text visible in submitted document; attachments list does not include it.
non_collusion_declaration.notes: RFP required a signed/dated non-collusion declaration. Owner should confirm attached in original PDF before ranking.

minimum_years_in_business.evidence: Cover letter, page 1: 'Founded in 2012'; Why Heritage section, page 9: '14 years in business'. RFP minimum is 10 years.
minimum_years_in_business.notes: Minor internal inconsistency: 'Founded in 2012' implies 13-14 yrs as of 2026. Clearly above 10-yr minimum.

similar_project_references.evidence: References section, page 6: four commercial/industrial roof replacements - Amazon YHM1 (185,000 sqft, 2024), Magnotta Winery (92,000 sqft, 2023), Prologis Park 407 (145,000 sqft, 2025), Apotex Pharmaceuticals (78,000 sqft, 2024, temperature-sensitive).
similar_project_references.notes: All four references are same building-code class (commercial/industrial), within 0.92x-2.18x of 85,000 sqft subject, completed 2023-2025. Named contacts provided on every reference; project dollar values not disclosed. RFP minimum 3 comparable met with margin.

site_visit_attendance.evidence: Cover letter, page 1: 'We attended the mandatory site visit on March 25, 2026, and conducted a detailed analysis of the existing conditions.'
site_visit_attendance.notes: Matches RFP section 8.1 mandatory site meeting date.

red_flags.description: Warranty offered is 20-year membrane NDL only, not total_system_ndl. RFP sections 9.6 and 3.1 require total_system_ndl (full assembly: membrane + insulation + flashings + labour to reinstall). Bidder does not attach a named system-warranty program (e.g., Carlisle Total System, Firestone Red Shield Platinum, Soprema Sopra-Garantie Mammouth Platinum).
red_flags.evidence: Warranty (Base Bid) section, page 3: '20-year NDL warranty on TPO membrane'. Attachments list: '20-Year and 30-Year NDL Warranty Sample Documentation' (membrane-level wording, not system-warranty program document).

red_flags.description: VE Option 5 proposes omitting cover board on a mechanically attached TPO over polyiso assembly. Cover board omission on commercial polyiso is a known critical deficiency (protects membrane from polyiso facer degradation, fastener backout, and hail). Bidder's claim that 'manufacturer does not require cover board' is not supported by an attached manufacturer letter.
red_flags.citation: fixture 02 section 4 (cover board on polyiso); CRCA bulletin on cover boards
red_flags.evidence: VE Option 5, page 5: 'Remove cover board (not required with mechanically attached assembly per manufacturer) = -$8,000'. No manufacturer letter attached confirming the exclusion for this system.

red_flags.description: Wind uplift design basis not stated. Commercial low-slope per OBC Part 3 / CSA A123.21 or FM 1-29 must have a stated wind uplift design. VE Option 1 asserts 'wind uplift risk is moderate' without quoting a design calculation or FM rating.
red_flags.evidence: VE Option 1, page 4: 'For a single-story industrial building in Mississauga with parapet walls, wind uplift risk is moderate.' Base bid Key Specifications table (page 3) has no wind uplift row.

red_flags.description: Fall protection plan is generic ('fall protection training for all workers') with no site-specific anchor points, tie-off plan, or parapet/perimeter strategy. For a 28-ft industrial roof with 47 penetrations, a site-specific fall-arrest plan per CSA Z91 is expected.
red_flags.citation: fixture 01 section 3 (fall protection); O. Reg. 297/13; CSA Z91
red_flags.evidence: Safety Program section, page 8 - bullet list only. No anchor-point diagram or site-specific tie-off description.

red_flags.description: Exclusion 'Work outside standard hours (7 AM - 6 PM weekdays)' conflicts with RFP requirement for weekend/off-hours weather protection response on an occupied pharma facility. Bidder's weekend protection plan uses passive tarps only; no provision for active response to weather events outside business hours.
red_flags.citation: RFP section 11 note 6 (phasing); fixture 03 section 5 (phasing occupied buildings)
red_flags.evidence: Exclusions item 6, page 7; contrasted with Phasing Commitments page 4 stating 'Weekend protection: reinforced tarps with weighted edges and secondary drainage' only.

red_flags.description: Deck repair allowances ($10,000 steel + $10,000 wood) are thin for a 1998 28-year-old BUR tear-off on 85,000 sqft industrial + office wing. Bidder also does not provide deck-replacement or flashing unit pricing, creating change-order exposure for extras beyond allowance.
red_flags.evidence: Price Breakdown page 2; Clarifications item 2, page 7.

red_flags.description: VE Option 1 framing is misleading: 'Same 20-year NDL warranty available' for a mechanically attached system. Mechanically attached TPO over polyiso without cover board (as bundled in Option 5) can void or disqualify manufacturer total-system warranty tiers absent written manufacturer approval.
red_flags.citation: fixture 02 sections 3, 4.5 (certified installer, system warranty prerequisites)
red_flags.evidence: VE Option 1, page 4; VE Option 5, page 5.

red_flags.description: Value-engineering narrative applies commercial pressure toward alternates ('VE process saved clients $2.3M'; 'BEST VALUE' language on Combined Optimal Package). Owner should judge base-bid compliance on its own and evaluate VE options separately, not as an implied discount.
red_flags.citation: fixture 03 section 2 (mandatory vs rated; best value vs low bid)
red_flags.evidence: Why Heritage section, page 9; VE Option 5 Combined Optimal Package, page 5.

red_flags.description: VE Option 6 proposes split-fiscal-year installation with winter-exposed deck - inconsistent with the temperature-sensitive pharma tenant. Listed but not recommended; owner should decline in writing if selecting base bid.
